title: Bounded constructibility of every finite-type direct image
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism between finite-type schemes over
a field $k$, and let $A$ be a finite ring annihilated by an
integer invertible in $k$. Then

$$
Rf_*:D^b_c(X,A)\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,A)
$$

is defined on the ordinary derived categories. The morphism
$f$ need not be separated.
The notation refers to bounded constructible complexes.

proof.text: A finite-type $k$-scheme has a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras. By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], each such spectrum is Noetherian; a finite union of Noetherian open subspaces is Noetherian, since a descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes on each member and hence globally. Thus $X$ and $Y$ are Noetherian and all their open subsets are quasi-compact. Choose a bounded-below injective representative $J^\bullet$ of $K$ using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. For an open immersion, restriction is exact: kernels are computed sectionwise, and a section of a sheaf cokernel is locally a section of the presheaf cokernel; the covering families in the localized site are the same families. Restriction preserves injectives by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized-adjunction]: its left adjoint preserves finite limits and colimits, hence is exact, and the adjunction turns the extension problem across a monomorphism into the extension problem for an injective. Restriction preserves zero morphisms since it is sectionwise. For an affine open $V\subset Y$, the restriction of $f_*J$ to $V$ equals $(f|_{f^{-1}V})_*(J|_{f^{-1}V})$: on an etale object $W\to V$ both are $J(W\times_Y X)$ by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Thus derived direct image restricts to the derived direct image over $V$. Choose a finite affine cover of $Y$. Finite unions of its cohomological bounds are bounded. Constructibility glues over this cover: refine each finite stratification by successive differences of the cover members, and concatenate the resulting finite stratifications. All these differences are constructible locally closed subsets in the Noetherian finite-type schemes. Restriction of a constructible sheaf is constructible by restricting its strata [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. It suffices to prove the assertion with $Y$ affine.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: locality on Y and finite affine covers

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $X_1,\ldots,X_r$ of $X$. If $X$ is empty then $K=0$ and the conclusion holds; otherwise take $r\ge1$. For each $i$, write $X_i=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$. A finite set of $k$-algebra generators of $B$ also generates it over $R$, so $X_i\to Y$ is of finite type. The morphism $X_i\to Y$ admits a compactification $X_i\hookrightarrow\overline X_i\xrightarrow{p_i}Y$ by [prop-nagata-affine-compactification], [def-nagata-affine-compactification], and [def-nagata-compactification]. This is the affine-space/projective-closure construction in the first blueprint paragraph, not the general Nagata theorem. For a nonempty index subset $I$, fix $i\in I$. The intersection $X_I=\bigcap_{t\in I}X_t$ is open in $X_i$, hence also open in $\overline X_i$; composing the two open inclusions identifies it with that open subscheme. Its map to $Y$ is $p_i j_I$. No affineness of $X_I$ is required. The schemes $X_I$ and $\overline X_i$ are of finite type over $k$: the first is an open of a Noetherian finite-type scheme and the second is proper over the finite-type scheme $Y$. Restrict $K$ to $X_I$. Apply [cor-fin-deligne-open-finite-coefficients] to $j_I$ and [lem-fin-proper-bounded-constructible] to $p_i$. Clause (5) of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] identifies $Rf_{I,*}(K|_{X_I})$ with $Rp_{i,*}Rj_{I,*}(K|_{X_I})$, so it is bounded constructible. Choose bounds $a_I,b_I$ for each of these finitely many complexes; empty intersections contribute zero and may be assigned any bounds.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: factor each affine-cover intersection through an open immersion and a projective morphism

proof.text: Let $u_I:X_I\hookrightarrow X$. In horizontal degree $p$ form $C^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{|I|=p+1}u_{I,*}(J^q|_{X_I})$, for $0\le p\le r-1$, with alternating restriction differential and augmentation $J^q\to C^{0,q}$. These augmented rows are exact. Indeed, over any cover member $X_t$ insert $t$ in an ordered index list, with the sign of its position, and put zero when $t$ already occurs; intersections with $X_t$ identify the resulting summands, and cancellation of the deletion/insertion terms gives $dh+hd=1$ for the augmented complex. These local contractions show sheaf exactness. Each row term is injective: restriction of $J^q$ is injective by step 1, and $u_{I,*}$ preserves injectives because it is right adjoint to exact open restriction [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; finite sums of injectives are injective. Starting with the augmented injective object $J^q$, split its monomorphism into $C^{0,q}$, then split the monomorphism of the injective complement into $C^{1,q}$, and continue. Thus the finite augmented row is split exact and remains exact after applying the additive functor $f_*$. Put $D^{p,q}=f_*C^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{|I|=p+1}f_{I,*}(J^q|_{X_I})$, using the section formula in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The augmentation $f_*J\to\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ is a quasi-isomorphism: in its augmented cone the horizontal rows are exact, the vertical degree is bounded below, and there are finitely many horizontal degrees. For a total cocycle, its component of lowest vertical degree is a horizontal cocycle; solve it using row exactness and subtract its total boundary. The new lowest component has larger vertical degree and smaller horizontal degree. Repeating at most $r+1$ times removes all components. This proves acyclicity of the cone. Hence $\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ represents $Rf_*K$. The total differential is $d_h+(-1)^p d_v$. To apply the first-quadrant definition [def-sp-double-complex-total], choose an integer $m$ with $J^q=0$ for $q<m$ and put $\widetilde D^{p,t}=D^{p,t+m}$ for $t\ge0$. This is first-quadrant, and define $\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=\operatorname{Tot}(\widetilde D)^{n-m}$ with the same differential. Its diagonal sums are finite because $0\le p\le r-1$. Reindexing back gives precisely the displayed total differential and the column degrees used below; this is degree reindexing, with no change to $K$ or its cohomological bounds.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: finite alternating Cech resolution applied to an injective resolution

proof.text:
Filter $\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ by the horizontal degree: $F^p\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=\bigoplus_{s\ge p}D^{s,n-s}$. The filtration is finite, with $F^0=\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ and $F^r=0$. Its graded complex in degree $p$ is the $p$-th column shifted by $p$, with differential $(-1)^p d_v$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Apply [lem-sp-bounded-filtered-page-core] in the abelian category of etale $A$-module sheaves: the required maps $F^p/F^{p+t}\to F^{p-t+1}/F^{p+1}$ for $t\ge1$ are induced by inclusion, since $F^{p+t}\subset F^{p+1}$. This gives a spectral sequence with
$$E_1^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{|I|=p+1}\mathcal H^q(Rf_{I,*}(K|_{X_I}))\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*K).$$
The column identifications use the restricted injective representative from step 1; changing the differential by the constant sign $(-1)^p$ changes neither kernels nor images. The cited finite-filtration theorem supplies page cohomology, stabilization and the finite filtration of the abutment. It applies to bounded-below vertical degree, not just degree zero sheaves; the Grothendieck spectral sequence for a composite of two direct images is not used here.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: the displayed Cech spectral sequence

proof.text: Set $a=\min_I a_I$ and $b=\max_I b_I$. The first page vanishes unless $0\le p\le r-1$ and $a\le q\le b$, so every later page has that support. By [thm-constructible-serre], finite sums of constructible sheaves are constructible (use the split short exact sequence for a sum), and the kernel modulo image defining each next page is constructible (the image is a kernel of a cokernel). Thus every stable-page term is constructible. The finite abutment filtration from step 4 has these terms as its successive quotients, so induction on its length using Serre closure under extensions proves that every $\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)$ is constructible. For $n<a$ or $n>b+r-1$ all its graded pieces vanish, so the finite filtration proves $\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)=0$. This is bounded constructibility by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. For $r=1$ the filtration has only its degree-zero column; for $K=0$ all pages are zero. Step 1 glues the result over the finite affine cover of $Y$.
